classification.difficultyReason: Infer the intersection from the total and neither count, then calculate probabilities for three events.

content.prompt: In a group of 200 students, 60 study geography, 80 study economics and 70 study neither.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent this information in a Venn diagram.

answer.short: Geography only: 50; both: 10; economics only: 70; neither: 70.
answer.worked:
The number studying at least one subject is $200-70=130$.

$$\begin{align*}n(G\cap E)&=60+80-130\\n(G\cap E)&=10\\n(G\text{ only})&=60-10\\n(G\text{ only})&=50\\n(E\text{ only})&=80-10\\n(E\text{ only})&=70\end{align*}$$

Place 70 outside both circles. Here $G$ represents geography and $E$ represents economics.
